source.title: QGen: On the Ability to Generalize in Quantization Aware Training
source.authors: Mohammadhossein Askarihemmat; Ahmadreza Jeddi; Reyhane Askari Hemmat; Ivan Lazarevich; Alexander Hoffman; Sudhakar Sah; Ehsan Saboori; Y. Savaria; Jean-Pierre David

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices; no apparent cutoff or garbling that prevents reading the relevant sections.
record.tranche_reason: Measures clean-distribution train–test loss gaps and magnitude-aware sharpness across quantization settings. This bears conceptually on V7, though the study does not use V7’s matched-training-loss comparison or test its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses random-label fitting only as cited prior work; it does not test random labels. Its distorted-data results concern corrupted inputs, outside the mapped versions’ in-distribution claims. Table 1 reports aggregate NiN results across 243 hyperparameter settings per dataset and precision. Table 3 reports several flatness metrics; rows below extract the magnitude-aware original-parameter PAC-Bayesian and sharpness metrics for the four NiN configurations.
record.test_reason: The study uses magnitude-aware sharpness as an indicator of generalization to evaluate quantization. It reports precision-level aggregate gaps and sharpness values for selected configurations, but does not pair those configurations with their gaps or evaluate whether sharpness ranks gaps among similarly low-training-loss networks. These results do not establish or contradict V7's relationship. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' conclusion: quantization acts as regularization, can facilitate flatter minima, and often reduces generalization gaps, including under corruption, with precision requiring tuning. Their generalization claims primarily concern loss gaps and should not be paraphrased as uniformly improved held-out accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: Uses quantization-aware training to study precision effects, not the magnitude-aware sharpness correlation experiment described in V7.
record.method_sensitivity: Quantization level changes training loss, test loss, generalization gap, and flatness measures; outcomes also vary by dataset and architecture. Distorted-data results vary by corruption severity, distortion, and model.

fits_no_version.finding: Lower-precision NiN models have smaller aggregate loss gaps, alongside worse training accuracy; CIFAR-10 test accuracy also decreases from 88.05% to 86.11% at Int2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Quantization can reduce train–test loss gaps while reducing fitting capacity and held-out accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: All four extracted NiN configurations have lower magnitude-aware PAC-Bayesian and sharpness complexities when quantized than at FP32.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Quantization-aware training can lower magnitude-aware sharpness-based complexity measures relative to full precision.

record.problems: The paper reports no uncertainty for the tabulated values. Table 1 aggregates NiN results over 243 hyperparameter settings per precision, and changes in precision also change training performance; therefore it does not isolate the relationship at matched training loss. The study does not report a correlation or ranking comparison between gap and the tested measures. Some claims about performance on corrupted data are outside the mapped versions.
record.rows_left_out: Table 3 includes additional unextracted measures (ordinary PAC-Bayesian and sharpness, and magnitude-aware Init variants) for the same NiN configurations and other architectures; omitted to keep the extraction focused on magnitude-aware original-parameter measures. Table 1 also reports DeiT-T, Swin-T, and ResNet-18 results on ImageNet-1K; omitted because the mapped V7 claim specifies a convolutional family comparison and these do not provide the same NiN aggregate setup. Table 4 and Appendix Tables 5–6 report corrupted-data gaps, outside the mapped versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label held-out performance under the same recipes.
Test error as width increases beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Held-out performance comparisons between adaptive optimizers and SGD under specified tuning budgets; optimizer choices are pooled here.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove their penalty.
Dropout effects and interactions with dataset size, augmentation, and weight decay.

Configuration-level association between magnitude-aware sharpness and generalization gaps at similarly low training loss; ranking against norm and margin measures. Precision-level gap averages cannot be paired with the selected configurations' sharpness values.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Remove both proposed V7 labels. The separate aggregate-gap and selected-configuration sharpness results do not establish support, and the absence of matched low training loss is an untested condition rather than a demonstrated scope limitation. Width and optimizer sweeps are pooled, so they supply no reported V2 or V4 comparison. No files or external sources were accessed.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization in the same training recipes.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation on natural labels.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer generalization comparisons as a claim about optimizer choice.
Large versus small batch size under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout and its interaction with augmentation or weight decay.

Matched similarly low training loss; CIFAR-10/SVHN without augmentation as a controlled family comparison; ranking against the tested norm- and margin-based measures; uncertainty for individual table values.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: NiN aggregate results on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 across quantization levels
reader_labels.reason: Quantized rows show lower reported generalization gaps than FP32, and magnitude-aware sharpness values are lower across the extracted NiN configurations (r2-r4, r6-r8, r10-r12, r14-r16, r18-r20, r22-r24, r26-r28, r30-r32, r34-r36, r38-r40). The study does not report a correlation test.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Training losses and accuracies change with precision, so the results do not establish the claimed relation among networks trained to similarly low loss; the selected sharpness values also do not directly rank gaps across matched-loss networks (r1-r8, r9-r40).
